reset: Reset puts the original workflow.json back.
title: A CI workflow that validates, tests and deploys a bundle
objective_text: Use the Databricks CLI in a CI workflow to validate and deploy bundles, with tests before deploy.
scenario: The team's CI workflow deploys the bundle before the tests run, signs in with an engineer's personal token pasted into the file, and runs on feature branches too. A broken change reached prod twice this month.
engine_label: A model of a CI workflow file, checked on this PC
verifies: Your workflow validates the bundle, runs the tests and only then deploys to the prod target, on pushes to main, signed in as a service principal with its secrets kept in the repository's secret store, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That the workflow runs: no CI system, CLI or workspace is used here, and the file is JSON, not a real workflow file.
Workload identity federation, which avoids a client secret altogether.

expected.description: Push to main only; DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID and DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET from secrets, no DATABRICKS_TOKEN; steps validate -t prod, pytest, deploy -t prod.

validation.pass: Validate, then tests, then deploy to prod.
validation.fail: The steps don't stop a bad change before it deploys.

rules.why: Validate catches a broken bundle before anything else runs.
Tests run before deploy, so a failing test stops the deploy.
With no -t the CLI uses the bundle's default target, which is dev.

validation.pass: Signed in as the service principal, with its secret kept out of the file.
validation.fail: The workflow signs in the wrong way.

rules.why: A secret written in the workflow file is in every clone of the repository.
Use a service principal, not a person's token, for CI/CD.

validation.pass: Only a push to main deploys to prod.
validation.fail: Another branch can deploy to prod.

explanation: Put the checks before the deploy: databricks bundle validate catches a broken bundle, the unit tests catch a broken transformation, and only then does databricks bundle deploy run, with -t prod because a deploy with no target goes to the bundle's default, dev. CI should sign in as a service principal, with DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID and DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET read from the repository's secrets, not as a person with a token pasted into the file, and only a push to main should deploy to prod.
hints: Steps run in order. Which ones must pass before anything is deployed?
databricks bundle deploy with no -t deploys to the default target.
${{ secrets.NAME }} reads a repository secret, so the value never appears in the file.
A service principal signs in with DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID and DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET; DATABRICKS_TOKEN is a personal access token.
